//: Security headers and SPA routing for the static frontend.
The API sets its own headers through Hono's secureHeaders middleware. This
file is the other half: the frontend is served straight from Vercel's CDN,
which means no application code runs on the way out and nothing was setting
The CSP is deliberately tight because this app needs almost nothing. No
third-party scripts, no external fonts, no analytics, no embedded frames.
The only host it talks to is the API, which is why connect-src is the one
directive with a placeholder to fill in at deploy time.
style-src carries 'unsafe-inline' and that is not an oversight: Vite emits
a stylesheet, but the rating dial sets its arc colour through an inline
style attribute, which CSP counts as inline styling. The alternative is a
nonce, and a nonce needs a server rendering the document — which is exactly
what a static CDN deploy does not have. Inline *styles* cannot execute; the
directive that matters for that is script-src, and it allows nothing but

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://crema-api.vercel.app; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests

headers.//: Hashed filenames, so these can be cached indefinitely.
The document is not hashed and must never be served stale, or a new deploy's index would still point at deleted assets.

rewrites.//: Client-side routing: every path renders the SPA, which is what makes a deep link work on a hard refresh rather than 404ing at the CDN.
